title: History and geography 6–8
purpose: Use geography skills and primary sources to study ancient civilizations, world religions and empires, the medieval and early modern world, and U.S. history to industrialization.

weeks.2: Early humans and the first civilizations
weeks.9: The American Revolution and the Constitution
weeks.10: The early republic and westward expansion

blocks.deliverable: Use latitude and longitude and explain why early cities grew near rivers.
Compare two ancient civilizations' governments and inventions.
Describe the beliefs and spread of three world religions in neutral terms.
Week 7 midterm; explain causes and effects of the Columbian Exchange, including disease.
Explain the main compromises of the Constitution.
Analyze a primary source from the Civil War or industrial era.
Submit the project; take an unseen 45 minute final in week 14.

project: Primary-source project: analyze three primary sources about one period and write a short historical argument that uses them as evidence.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
